newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices edge up at start, outlook stable.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices edge up at start, outlook stable.

text.p: Danish bond prices nudged up a little in early trading on Thursday but dealers predicted little change in a becalmed, stable market ahead of the Friday national holiday when the bourse will be closed.
"Prices are at a stable level, we do not expect much movement today, there's no real market-moving news expected so it will probably be pretty quiet up to the holiday," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 opened up a marginal 0.07 point from Wednesday's close at 109.59.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 70. The crown traded at 3.8092 per mark at 0725 gmt firming from Wednesday's closing 3.8100.
